clue.text: Pre-arranged exercises or studies

indicators.note: arranged here means the three letters of the clue's 'Pre' are put into a new order

parts.note: to exercise a right or skill is to use it, so exercises gives uses

explanation.surface: A fitness routine planned in advance, or perhaps some academic work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pre-arranged' looks like one word meaning planned, but it splits: 'arranged' rearranges PRE into PER, then USES follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To read something carefully is to study it, a close synonym.

clue.text: Spouter's revolutionary attitude

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests turning things over, so the letters of the clue's spouter are reordered

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A ranting orator holds radical political views.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' seems to describe the spouter's politics but is the anagram signal; the possessive 's adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A stance or bearing, physical or mental, is an attitude.

clue.text: Get one's own back

parts.note: reads as the idiom for taking revenge, but literally means recovering goods that belong to you

explanation.definitionFit: Retaking property, such as a car on unpaid finance, is literally getting your own things back.

clue.text: Taking a seaman round a port in Uruguay

parts.note: an old salt is an experienced sailor
the letter O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A sailor is being shown around a South American harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: SALTO is a city on the Uruguay River in north-west Uruguay. 'Taking' only joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Salto is a river port in Uruguay, named geographically.

clue.text: A tourist found these girls sadly without any money

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters of these girls are jumbled once one letter is set aside

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for the pound, from Latin libra, so money gives L

explanation.surface: A traveller discovers some young women have been left penniless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' scrambles THESE GIRLS and 'without' removes L (the pound sterling, from Latin libra), leaving the nine letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone visiting places of interest for pleasure is a tourist.

clue.text: Lay about cheat, not saying very much

indicators.note: about means the word for lay wraps around the word for cheat

parts.note: lay, meaning not of the clergy, is laic
to con someone is to cheat them

explanation.surface: A layabout swindler who keeps quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay about' reads as layabout, an idler, but splits into LAIC with 'about' putting it round CON.
explanation.definitionFit: A terse, sparing speaker uses few words.

clue.text: Inflation is breaking the Lord, a Scottish owner

indicators.note: breaking means splitting open the Lord abbreviation to let the other piece in

parts.note: a tyre is inflated with air

explanation.surface: Rising prices are ruining an aristocratic Scottish landowner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inflation' suggests economics, but it is AIR pumped into a tyre, here inside LD.
explanation.definitionFit: A laird is a Scottish landed proprietor, the owner of an estate.

clue.text: Quite unperturbed, it's gathered

definitions.meaning: calm and composed, in full control of oneself

explanation.surface: Someone serenely calm while things are being picked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Composed and calm in temperament; also assembled or amassed, like stamps by a hobbyist.

clue.text: She was very tearful in retiring with honour

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the word in is read backwards

parts.note: the OBE, Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

explanation.surface: A woman wept when she stepped down with a decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth NIOBE lost all her children and was turned to a stone that kept weeping.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical mother whose grief made her weep endlessly is the type of a tearful woman.

clue.text: A flowery word from the poet?

definitions.meaning: the name of a pink or white wildflower
the surname of the Elizabethan poet and lutenist Thomas ...

explanation.definitionFit: A wildflower of the pink family; also the surname of the English poet and composer Thomas Campion.

clue.text: Bit of a bloomer, going to sea without a mate

indicators.note: without means the letter a is dropped from the word sea

parts.note: taken as written
a mate is a friend or pal

explanation.surface: A sailor sets off alone with no companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without a mate' reads as one phrase, but 'without a' trims SEA to SE and 'mate' gives PAL. A 'bloomer' is a flower, not a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A leafy part of a flower's outer whorl, a component of a blossom.

clue.text: The newly-wed will accept only a little water in the restaurant

indicators.note: accept means the bridegroom word takes the stream word inside it

parts.note: a groom is a man just married
a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: A new husband agrees to have only a sip of water while dining out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'water' suggests a drink, but it is a RILL, a tiny stream, placed inside GROOM.
explanation.definitionFit: An eating place serving grilled food is a kind of dining establishment.

clue.text: Never seen so clean!

definitions.meaning: not noticed or observed by anyone

explanation.surface: An exclamation about something astonishingly spotless.
explanation.definitionFit: Unnoticed by any observer; also without a stain, blemish or mark.

clue.text: Some fruit peel emits a fragrant substance

indicators.note: some means only a portion of the words fruit peel emits is taken

explanation.surface: Citrus rind gives off a pleasant aroma.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' asks for a run of letters inside 'peel emits'.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemi is an aromatic resin from tropical trees used in varnishes and perfumes.

clue.text: Standing to attention before the court

parts.note: ere is an old word meaning before
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: Someone stands stiffly before a judge.
explanation.definitionFit: Upright and rigid, the posture of a soldier at attention.

clue.text: Like Herrick's Rose, incapable of scoring!

definitions.meaning: Robert Herrick wrote of a rose without prickles
unable to scratch or mark, since to score is to scratch

explanation.definitionFit: A rose lacking prickles, as in Herrick's poem, cannot scratch, and to score is to mark with a scratch.

clue.text: Regards transport as a painful sight

parts.note: to regard is to look at, so regards gives eyes, as a verb
a train is a means of transport

explanation.surface: Someone thinks public transport is an unpleasant spectacle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a painful sight' sounds like an eyesore but means sight, the faculty, made painful.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatigue or ache of vision from overuse is literally pain in one's seeing.

clue.text: Possibly rue never being other than environmentally-aware

parts.note: never being other than means always, which is ever
green means concerned for the environment

explanation.surface: Someone may regret always having been an eco-warrior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rue' looks like the verb regret, but it is the shrub rue, which keeps its leaves all year.
explanation.definitionFit: Rue is a herb that keeps its leaves through winter, an example of such a plant.

clue.text: Acknowledging a young woman in a seedy club

indicators.note: in means the young woman is placed inside the club word

parts.note: a dive is a disreputable bar or nightclub
miss is a title for a young unmarried woman

explanation.surface: Someone owns up to meeting a girl in a sleazy nightspot.
explanation.definitionFit: Inclined to admit or concede, which is to acknowledge.

clue.text: Talk of the underworld and run!

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and the realm itself
to course is to run or flow

explanation.surface: A conversation about gangsters, followed by a hasty escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underworld' suggests criminals, but it is DIS, the classical realm of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken or written discussion is a formal word for conversation.

clue.text: Cut time for the accommodation of ships

parts.note: to dock is to cut short, as with a tail or wages
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A reduced period for berthing vessels in harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Berthing space for vessels, or the fee charged for it, at a quay.

clue.text: Showing spirit, a leading journalist backed protest

indicators.note: backed means the joined pieces are read from end to start

parts.note: rum is a spirit drink
ED is short for editor, the chief journalist

explanation.surface: A senior newspaperman shows courage in supporting a demonstration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' looks like support, but it turns RUMED round as a whole. 'Showing' and 'a' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: To object or raise a doubt is to make a mild protest.

clue.text: Dire use may be made of the remains

indicators.note: may be made suggests something formed from these letters, so dire use is rearranged

explanation.surface: Leftovers might be put to dreadful use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be made' signals that DIRE USE is rearranged; 'of' joins it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: What is left over after the rest is removed is the remains.

clue.text: Stop to read about the forerunners of Osbert Lancaster

indicators.note: about means the study word wraps around the initials

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or read carefully

indicators.note: forerunners are what come first, so the initial letters of Osbert and Lancaster are taken

explanation.surface: Someone pauses to read up on the predecessors of the cartoonist Osbert Lancaster.
explanation.walkthrough: Osbert Lancaster was a British cartoonist. 'Stop' is a punctuation mark, not a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: A colon is a punctuation mark, and such marks were once called stops.

clue.text: Record one century in the science of thought

parts.note: a log is a written record, such as a ship's log
I is the Roman numeral one
C is the Roman numeral 100 and the cricket abbreviation for a century

explanation.surface: A writer jots down one hundred years of the study of reasoning.
explanation.definitionFit: The study of valid reasoning and inference is the discipline of correct thinking.

clue.text: Traffic indicators

parts.note: reads as car turn signals, but means the roadside boards that point the way

explanation.definitionFit: Roadside boards that point drivers toward destinations guide motorists.

clue.text: A good man with experience

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint, a good man
and means together with

explanation.surface: A virtuous person who has seen a lot of life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'experience' is the definition as a verb: to go through or endure something.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure or undergo something, as in 'stand trial', is to go through it.

clue.text: Hand round a soft fruit

indicators.note: round means the hand word goes around the other letters

parts.note: a paw is a hand, informally
p, short for piano, means soft in music

explanation.surface: Someone passes around a squashy piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soft fruit' reads as one phrase, but 'soft' is P (piano), placed with A inside PAW.
explanation.definitionFit: A papaw is a tropical fruit, another name for the papaya.

clue.text: A great egg concoction to get together

indicators.note: a concoction is something mixed up, so the letters of a great egg are mixed

explanation.surface: A fine egg dish whipped up for a gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: To collect into a mass or whole is to gather together.

clue.text: Looked for sound self-esteem

indicators.note: sound tells us to go by how the word is pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: pride is self-respect or self-esteem

explanation.surface: Someone searched for a healthy sense of self-worth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective meaning healthy but signals that PRIDE is pronounced like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To peer or snoop nosily is to look inquisitively.

clue.text: Finish up without a suit packed

indicators.note: without means outside, so the finish word surrounds the suit word

parts.note: to end is to finish up
a lawsuit is a legal case

explanation.surface: Someone ends up without any clothes in their luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, an old sense, not lacking. 'suit' is a lawsuit, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Enclosed in a covering or container, as goods are when boxed.

clue.text: Not existing in any locale or doubly present?

parts.note: present in time is now, and present in place is here, so the phrase gives two words
present in time is now, and present in place is here, so the phrase gives two words

explanation.surface: Something both absent everywhere and somehow present twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubly present' uses both senses of present: in time and in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Located in no place at all; absent from every location.
